domain: Battle action/ability resolution tail: elemental-power roll, ability-kind classification (attack/unleash/psynergy family codes), success-rate gating, per-target power step accumulation, jump-table power-tier lookup, djinn-summon power table application, and per-target hit-power writing for one battle action.
blocking_finding: Region_080bef88 is not a standalone function. Its retained assembly begins directly with `ldr r3, [sp, #12]` -- no push, no stack allocation -- yet its epilogue restores four callee-saved registers (r8-r11) plus lr via a pop/mov-shuffle sequence that was never pushed anywhere in this owner's 608 bytes. The matching prologue does not exist at this address. Tracing the call graph shows why: the immediately preceding owner, games/gs1/asm/080beb08.s, also begins with no push (`mov r2, r10` as its first instruction) and reaches this owner only via a plain conditional branch (`bne sub_080bef88`, the literal final instruction of 080beb08.s) -- not `bl`. 080beb08.s itself is reached the same way from games/gs1/asm/080be76c.s, which also opens with no push (`ldr r4, [sp, #12]`) and already treats r9, r10, r11 as live incoming state. All three owners (080be76c, 080beb08, 080bef88), plus their forward siblings 080bf678 and 080bfba4 (both referenced by absolute-address branches from this owner and from 080beb08), are internal branch targets of one very large enclosing function whose real entry (push of r4-r11 equivalent plus lr, and its stack-frame allocation) lies at an address earlier than 080be76c that was not in scope for this task. None of the five sibling owners in this call-graph-reachable region currently has any candidate C or json, and none is registered in games/gs1/recon/translation-units.json.
why_this_caps_the_score: GCC 2.96 cannot emit a function whose body performs multiple `bl` calls and uses four callee-saved high registers (r8-r11) with zero prologue -- `bl` clobbers lr, so any non-leaf function must save it before the first call, and any use of r8-r11 across a call requires them to be pushed (via the low-register mov-shuffle idiom, which is exactly what this owner's own epilogue performs on the way out). Every ordinary top-level C function compiles to a real prologue at its entry point. The 608-byte reference has no prologue at 0x080bef88, so no top-level C function reconstruction of this owner in isolation can ever reach differing_halfwords=0; the mismatch is present in the very first emitted instruction regardless of body content.

attempts.note: Baseline: confirms reference content is 608 bytes of real logic starting immediately, with no room for any prologue.

attempts.candidate: full best-effort translation of the observed logic (elemental roll, ability-kind switch/dispatch, per-target power accumulation loop) as a 3-argument standalone function
attempts.note: GCC emits the expected `push {r5,r6,r7,lr}; mov r7,r8; push {r7}` prologue as instruction 1-3, which the reference does not have at any point. Confirms the mismatch is structural (missing shared frame), not a body/logic/type problem -- register-allocator and body changes cannot remove a prologue the reference never had.

refuted_hypotheses: That Region_080bef88 is a normal, independently callable function reached via `bl` -- refuted: every real cross-reference to this address and to its immediate predecessor/successor owners in games/gs1/asm/*.s uses a bare conditional or unconditional branch (`b`/`bne`), never `bl`, and the only owner in this cluster with a real prologue was not located within the searched call graph.

That a leaf-style or reduced-register-pressure rewrite of the body could remove the prologue -- refuted by the second attempt: the body genuinely calls into 7 external functions and needs 2+ values (an elemental-power actor id and a target-power sign/kind) live across those calls, which GCC 2.96 can only keep in callee-saved registers, forcing the same class of prologue regardless of phrasing.

That forcing a `naked`/prologue-less function via project-approved means could resolve this -- not attempted: CONTRIBUTING.md and Cleanroom's ordinary-C89 rule prohibit fixed-register variables, empty barriers, and other escape hatches used to fake a shape the compiler would not otherwise emit; a naked function is exactly such an escape hatch.
recommendation: This owner cannot be adopted independently. It must be reconstructed together with its full enclosing function, which spans at minimum games/gs1/asm/080be76c.s, games/gs1/asm/080beb08.s, games/gs1/asm/080bef88.s, and (via absolute-address branches observed in this owner and 080beb08) games/gs1/asm/080bf678.s and games/gs1/asm/080bfba4.s, plus whatever earlier owner holds the real prologue reached only by `bl` from outside this cluster (not identified in this session). The correct route per CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Translation units with holes' section is to scaffold a translation unit over that whole address range with `bun tools/unit-scaffold/scaffold.ts`, then reconstruct the enclosing function as one candidate and score every member owner from the same compiled object with `candidate-show --unit`. That scaffolding step was out of scope for this task (games/gs1/recon/translation-units.json is explicitly off-limits here) and is left for a follow-up with the correct scope.
